title: Transverse fields, helicity and angular momentum

items.title: Classical transverse Fourier amplitudes
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; authored for batch 9; independent review pending
items.statement:
Use a fixed positively oriented inertial laboratory chart with spatial coordinate
$x\in\mathbb R^3$, time $t\in\mathbb R$, Euclidean dot and cross products, and
the SI vacuum speed $c>0$. A smooth amplitude is a map
$a:\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}\to\mathbb C^3$ whose coordinate partial
derivatives of every order exist and are continuous. Require its support
$K\subset\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ to be compact and require the bilinear
transversality condition
$k\cdot a(k):=\sum_{j=1}^3 k_j a_j(k)=0$ for every $k\ne0$. The dot in this
condition is bilinear, with no complex conjugation. The zero extension of $a$
to $k=0$ is understood.

For a compactly supported continuous integrand, write its integral over
$\mathbb R^3$ for its Riemann integral over any sufficiently large cube
$[-R,R]^3$ containing its support; this value is independent of such $R$. Define
the complex vector potential and its associated real fields by

$$A_+(x,t):=(2\pi)^{-3/2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}a(k)\exp\!\bigl(i(k\cdot x-c|k|t)\bigr)\,d^3k,\qquad A:=2\operatorname{Re}A_+,\qquad \varphi:=0,\qquad E:=-\partial_tA,\qquad B:=\operatorname{curl}A.$$

Here $k$ is a spatial wavevector with units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, $|k|$ is its
Euclidean norm, $t$ is in seconds, and $i^2=-1$; thus the phase is
dimensionless and real part is taken componentwise.
If $a$ carries units $\mathrm{T\,m^4}$, then $A$ carries $\mathrm{T\,m}$,
$E$ carries $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, and $B$ carries $\mathrm T$. These fields are
real and jointly smooth on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$; at each fixed time
$A,E,B$ are Schwartz functions of $x$, and their spatial Schwartz seminorms are
bounded on every compact time interval. They satisfy the smooth source-free
vacuum Maxwell equations and the Coulomb condition
$\operatorname{div}A=0$ with the stated scalar potential $\varphi=0$. Their
total field energy
$W(t):=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{[-R,R]^3}u(x,t)\,d^3x$, with $u$ the vacuum
energy density, is finite for every $t$. The amplitudes are a classical Fourier
description; no photon state is defined.
items.physical_scope: Conditional classical vacuum electromagnetism in a fixed, positively oriented inertial laboratory chart on all of R^3, with SI units and the smooth source-free Maxwell branch. The item defines real finite-energy Schwartz fields from smooth compactly supported transverse Fourier amplitudes whose support excludes zero frequency, in the Coulomb gauge with scalar potential zero. It makes no empirical claim and assigns no one-photon Hilbert-space or quantized interpretation.

references.title: K. Y. Bliokh, F. J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, F. Nori and A. V. Zayats, Spin-orbit interactions of light, Nature Photonics 9 (2015), arXiv:1505.02864
references.locator: Section 'Angular momenta and geometric phases', especially the transverse-polarization and direction-dependent discussion in PDF pp. 3–5; this item proves its compact-support Fourier construction and regularity directly.

references.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, ETH Zürich 2024 FS lecture notes
references.locator: §11.1 'Anfangswertproblem', subsection 'Fourier-Raum', equations (11.5)–(11.10): the source-free Fourier mode representation and its transverse amplitude equations. Compact spectral support and Schwartz decay are established here directly.

items.title: Exact helicity projectors in vacuum
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; authored for batch 9; independent review pending
items.statement:
For $k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, let $n:=k/|k|$ and let the complex
transverse fibre be
$T_k:=\{v\in\mathbb C^3:\sum_j k_jv_j=0\}$. On $\mathbb C^3$ define
$C(k)v:=i\,n\times v$ and
$P_T(k)v:=v-n\sum_j n_jv_j$. Define
$P_\sigma(k):=\tfrac12(P_T(k)+\sigma C(k))$ for $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$.
Use the Hermitian product
$\langle u,v\rangle_H:=\sum_j\overline{u_j}v_j$. Then $P_T(k)$ is the
orthogonal projection onto $T_k$; $C(k)$ is Hermitian, vanishes on the
longitudinal line, and satisfies $C(k)^2=P_T(k)$. The restrictions of
$P_{+1}(k)$ and $P_{-1}(k)$ to $T_k$ are orthogonal rank-one projections with
sum $P_T(k)$. Their ranges are the two helicity eigenspaces, with eigenvalues
$+1$ and $-1$ for $C(k)$.

For a smooth compactly supported transverse amplitude $a(k)$ whose support
avoids $0$, define the Fourier multipliers
$(M_\sigma a)(k):=P_\sigma(k)a(k)$ and vacuum evolution
$(U_ta)(k):=e^{-ic|k|t}a(k)$. Both preserve this amplitude class and
$M_\sigma U_t=U_tM_\sigma$. For each proper rotation $R\in SO(3)$, where
$SO(3):=\{R\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}:R^TR=I,\det R=1\}$, define
$(R_*a)(k):=R a(R^Tk)$. Then $M_\sigma R_*=R_*M_\sigma$. The formula for
$P_\sigma(k)$ is globally smooth on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$; no globally
smooth nonvanishing polarization vector is asserted.
items.physical_scope: Conditional classical source-free vacuum electromagnetism in the fixed SI inertial laboratory chart. Helicity is the plus or minus eigenvalue of the stated operator on each nonzero transverse Fourier mode. No global smooth polarization basis, photon Hilbert space, position operator, material medium, or empirical claim is assumed.

references.title: K. Y. Bliokh, F. J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, F. Nori and A. V. Zayats, Spin-orbit interactions of light, Nature Photonics 9 (2015), arXiv:1505.02864
references.locator: Section 'Angular momenta and geometric phases', Boxes 1–2, PDF pp. 3–5: helicity labels, transverse polarization, and direction-dependent geometric phases. The projector identities here are proved directly.

references.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, ETH Zürich 2024 FS lecture notes
references.locator: §11.1 'Anfangswertproblem', subsection 'Fourier-Raum', equations (11.5)–(11.10): transverse source-free Fourier modes with dispersion ω=c|k|. The helicity eigenspace calculation here is local.

items.title: Coulomb-gauge canonical and kinetic integrals
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; authored for batch 9; independent review pending
items.statement:
Let $A,E,B:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be any fixed-time fields from the
compactly supported transverse Fourier construction: $A,E,B$ are real Schwartz
fields, $\operatorname{div}A=0$, $B=\operatorname{curl}A$, and
$\operatorname{div}E=0$. Use the positively oriented laboratory coordinates
$x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ and the fixed origin $0$. For every all-space integral below,
define it as the limit of the Riemann integrals over $Q_R=[-R,R]^3$ as
$R\to\infty$; the estimates in the Verification show absolute convergence.
For each scalar component $A_i$, define
$(x\times\nabla)A_i$ to have components
$\sum_{m,j=1}^3\epsilon_{\ell m j}x_m\partial_jA_i$, where
$\epsilon_{\ell m j}$ is the right-handed Levi-Civita symbol in this chart.
Define the total kinetic angular-momentum functional and its Coulomb-gauge
canonical orbital and spin functionals by

$$J_{\mathrm{kin}}:=\varepsilon_0\int_{\mathbb R^3}x\times(E\times B)\,d^3x,\qquad L_{\mathrm{can}}:=\varepsilon_0\sum_{i=1}^3\int_{\mathbb R^3}E_i(x\times\nabla)A_i\,d^3x,\qquad S_{\mathrm{can}}:=\varepsilon_0\int_{\mathbb R^3}E\times A\,d^3x.$$

Each is a finite vector with SI units $\mathrm{J\,s}$. The words “kinetic,”
“canonical orbital,” and “spin” are names for these functionals on this fixed
potential class; they do not identify three separately gauge-invariant local
densities. A generic gauge transform is outside this definition's domain.
items.physical_scope: Conditional classical vacuum electromagnetism in the fixed SI laboratory chart, restricted to the real Schwartz Fourier-packet fields and the particular Coulomb-gauge potential constructed on the preceding A page. The item defines global angular-momentum functionals relative to the fixed spatial origin. It does not assert that the separate terms are local, gauge-independent, universally measurable, or defined for non-decaying plane waves.

references.title: K. Y. Bliokh, F. J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, F. Nori and A. V. Zayats, Spin-orbit interactions of light, Nature Photonics 9 (2015), arXiv:1505.02864
references.locator: Section 'Angular momenta and geometric phases', Box 1, PDF pp. 3–4: the source distinguishes polarization/helicity contributions from spatial orbital contributions. The exact Coulomb-gauge integral identity here is derived locally.

references.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, ETH Zürich 2024 FS lecture notes
references.locator: §8.2, equations (8.15) and (8.18), and §8.3 'Drehimpuls, Schwerpunkt', equations (8.19)–(8.20): the SI momentum density, stress tensor and total origin-relative field angular momentum integral. The potential-dependent split is proved locally.

items.title: Equality of total angular momentum integrals
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; authored for batch 9; independent review pending
items.statement:
(a) For the real Schwartz vacuum fields and the fixed Coulomb-gauge potential
defined in the preceding A-page item, let $J_{\mathrm{kin}}$,
$L_{\mathrm{can}}$, and $S_{\mathrm{can}}$ be the three global functionals in
that definition. Then

$$J_{\mathrm{kin}}=L_{\mathrm{can}}+S_{\mathrm{can}}.$$

(b) More generally, let $R>0$ and let $E,A:\overline{Q_R}\to\mathbb R^3$ be restrictions of
$C^1$ maps on a neighborhood of the cube $Q_R=[-R,R]^3$, let
$B=\operatorname{curl}A$, and define
$$J_R:=\varepsilon_0\int_{Q_R}x\times(E\times B)\,d^3x,\quad L_R:=\varepsilon_0\sum_{i=1}^3\int_{Q_R}E_i(x\times\nabla)A_i\,d^3x,\quad S_R:=\varepsilon_0\int_{Q_R}E\times A\,d^3x.$$
For each component $\ell\in\{1,2,3\}$,

$$ (J_R)_\ell=(L_R)_\ell+(S_R)_\ell+\varepsilon_0\int_{Q_R}(\operatorname{div}E)(x\times A)_\ell\,d^3x-\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial Q_R}(n\cdot E)(x\times A)_\ell\,dS. $$

The boundary integral is the sum of the ordinary two-dimensional Riemann
integrals over the six faces with their outward unit normals $n$. If the volume
integrals converge absolutely and this boundary term tends to zero as
$R\to\infty$, the corresponding whole-space identity retains the term
$\varepsilon_0\int_{\mathbb R^3}(\operatorname{div}E)(x\times A)\,d^3x$.
Thus the source-free Schwartz equality in (a) uses both
$\operatorname{div}E=0$ and the vanishing surface limit; it is not an equality
of local densities.
items.physical_scope: Exact conditional identities for smooth classical electric fields and the stated vector potential in the fixed inertial SI laboratory chart. The all-space equality is restricted to source-free Schwartz vacuum packets in the specified Coulomb gauge. The finite-cube formula explicitly retains the divergence and boundary terms; no density-wise equality or universal gauge-independent split is claimed.

references.title: K. Y. Bliokh, F. J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, F. Nori and A. V. Zayats, Spin-orbit interactions of light, Nature Photonics 9 (2015), arXiv:1505.02864
references.locator: Section 'Angular momenta and geometric phases', Box 1, PDF pp. 3–4; contextual discussion only. The global identity and its boundary term are proved by componentwise integration by parts here.

references.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, ETH Zürich 2024 FS lecture notes
references.locator: §8.3 'Drehimpuls, Schwerpunkt', equations (8.19)–(8.20): the total field angular momentum is the integral of x crossed with field momentum density. The potential-dependent split is proved locally.

title: Transverse fields, helicity and angular momentum — Examples

items.title: Infinite plane waves have no total angular-momentum integral
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; authored for batch 9; independent review pending
items.statement:
Every nonzero monochromatic plane wave in vacuum belongs to the Schwartz
Fourier-packet domain on which the all-space angular-momentum functionals are
defined.
items.physical_scope: Ideal nonzero monochromatic plane waves in source-free classical vacuum electromagnetism on all of R^3, in the SI laboratory chart. The claim concerns only the domain of finite-energy total angular-momentum functionals; it does not reinterpret a plane wave by box normalization or claim a finite-beam approximation.

references.title: K. Y. Bliokh, F. J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, F. Nori and A. V. Zayats, Spin-orbit interactions of light, Nature Photonics 9 (2015), arXiv:1505.02864
references.locator: Section 'Angular momenta and geometric phases', Box 1, PDF pp. 3–4: beam angular-momentum descriptions are for structured/paraxial fields; this counterexample concerns the all-space domain of the stated classical functionals.

references.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, ETH Zürich 2024 FS lecture notes
references.locator: §8.2, equation (8.3), and §11.1 'Fourier-Raum', equations (11.5)–(11.10): the field energy density and ideal source-free Fourier modes. The infinite-energy conclusion is taken from the inspected local theorem.

items.title: Charged configurations retain an additional term
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; authored for batch 9; independent review pending
items.statement:
Let $\chi$ be the smooth cutoff equal to $1$ on the unit ball and $0$ outside
the radius-two ball. Every integral over $\mathbb R^3$ below means integration
over any cube containing the compact support of its integrand; the value is
independent of the chosen cube. Fix $L>0$ metres, $E_0>0$ volts per metre, and $A_0>0$
tesla metres, and put $f(x):=\chi(x/L)$ and $g(x):=\chi(x/(2L))$. For all
$(x,t)\in\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, define

$$E(x,t):=E_0f(x)e_1,\qquad A(x,t):=A_0g(x)e_2-tE_0f(x)e_1,\qquad \varphi:=0,\qquad B:=\operatorname{curl}A,\qquad \rho:=\varepsilon_0E_0\partial_1f,\qquad J:=\mu_0^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B.$$

These maps are smooth, compactly supported in space, and satisfy all four
smooth-branch Maxwell equations. At $t=0$ the boundary term in the finite-cube
angular-momentum identity vanishes, but the charge correction is

$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\,x\times A(x,0)\,d^3x=-\varepsilon_0E_0A_0L^3\left(\int_{\mathbb R^3}\chi(y)\,d^3y\right)e_3\ne0.$$

Thus the source-free total-integral equality cannot be extended to these
sourced fields by deleting the divergence term. This is a model calculation,
not a reported measurement.
items.physical_scope: A smooth sourced vacuum Maxwell solution in the SI laboratory chart, used only to demonstrate the divergence term in the componentwise angular-momentum identity. The displayed algebraic integrals extend the A-page formulas for this calculation; the example does not extend the A-page functionals' source-free Schwartz domain or make a gauge-invariant claim for general charged fields.

references.title: K. Y. Bliokh, F. J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, F. Nori and A. V. Zayats, Spin-orbit interactions of light, Nature Photonics 9 (2015), arXiv:1505.02864
references.locator: Section 'Angular momenta and geometric phases', Box 1, PDF pp. 3–4: context for keeping gauge and domain restrictions explicit; this sourced time-slice calculation is proved locally.

references.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, ETH Zürich 2024 FS lecture notes
references.locator: §8.2, equations (8.15) and (8.18), and §8.3 'Drehimpuls, Schwerpunkt', equations (8.19)–(8.20): field momentum and origin-relative angular momentum; the charge-supported correction is derived locally.
